title: Edtech platform raises $4.5M to help teach students how to vibe code
slides: Can an edtech platform make coding feel like play?
This startup just raised $4.5M for a new method.
Students learn by vibing code, not writing syntax.
Teachers now assign projects without lesson plans.
Try one free session—and watch your class engage.
thread_text:
1. Coding without typing?

An edtech startup just raised $4.5M to let students learn by “vibing” code — no syntax required.

2. Teachers skip lesson plans.

Assignments now run on the platform’s method, not a teacher’s prep time. Projects create themselves.

3. What happens to debugging?

If students never write syntax, they also never break it. No error messages means a new kind of fluency.

4. The classroom flips.

Teachers become facilitators. Students explore by feel, not instruction. The role of “lecturer” fades.

5. Try one free session.

Book a trial this week. If your class doesn’t engage more than last month, drop it. Would you risk 30 minutes?
